units.title: Storm clear-up. Damage reports and offers of help in this thread, please.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Good morning. To keep the General board readable, please post storm damage, road blockages and offers of help in this thread rather than starting new ones. Please include where you are. Do not post pictures of other people's houses without asking them, and please report fallen lines to the co-op, not to us. Thank you. Pell (admin).

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Station summary for the storm, Carrow Point. Lowest pressure 971.4 hPa just after 02:00 yesterday. Peak gust 61 knots at 23:50 the night before, which beats the Met Office's headland figure by two knots, not that I'm counting. Rain total over three days 68.2 mm. Pressure now rising 2.1 hPa an hour. The anemometer cup I lost on day one turned up in the hedge, so the readings after that are from the spare.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Storm clear up, fallen trees cut and stacked, fully insured, chainsaw tickets CS30 CS31 and CS38 (aerial), own tipper and chipper. Domestic or farm, no job too small. Tollinby, brackwater and Port ammet areas. Reasonable rates, can start today. Ring or message, Davey.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Davey, I'll allow one advert in here given the circumstances, but please put any further ones in Trades & Jobs. People are using this thread to find out whether their road is open. Thank you.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Lower Tollinby rd shut at Mill Bridge, beech down and half the verge in the beck. Diversion via the B-road past the quarry adds 15 min. Brackwater ridge rd also shut both ends. And the temp lights at the Brackwater jct are still on red, storm or no storm, they'll outlive us all.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Gilliver. Sea over the wall twice on the big tides. Inner harbour lost the little green rowing boat off the north steps, painter snapped. Coastguard has a boat adrift south of the harbour, likely the same. If anyone on the Holm side sees it on the shore, it's Jamie Tregear's, he'd be glad of it back.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby, Orchard Close. Power was off 19 hours. Things learned: 1. a full chest freezer stays frozen about a day if nobody opens it. 2. three children will open it. 3. you can cook fish fingers on a camping stove if you are brave. Back on now. Thank you to the lineman in the yellow jacket who waved at my youngest, she has talked about nothing else.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Lisle came through quite well, though the pier lights were out for most of the second night and the school field is now a pond. Mr Bram, I hope Jamie gets his boat back. I taught his father, who also lost a boat once, though in his case he lent it to a cousin and forgot.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Tollinby forecourt lost three bunting lines and a sign saying 'Finance Available'. If anyone finds it, keep it, I've got four more. Honestly the way people are going on you'd think nobody's seen wind before. It's the Sound. It blows.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: Thank you Bram for checking on me. The front window rattled all night but the lamp stayed lit, which was the main thing. My neighbour's garden gate is in my garden now. I have told him he can collect it when he likes, there is no hurry, it is a nicce gate.

units.title: Blue bins: the lorry has returned.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: At 07:12 this morning the recycling lorry came down Rope Walk for the first time in three weeks. I have it on my watch. The council newsletter promised 'a short interruption'. Three weeks is not short. However, credit where due: the crew took the extra bags as promised and put my lid back the right way round. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Congratulations Bernard. Here in Weyhaven our block's bins are emptied by a private firm the landlord pays, who come when they please. Last week it was Tuesday at 05:00, reversing alarm and all, then nothing for nine days. I have written to the landlord. I will write again. One of us has to.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Glad for you Bernard. Tollinby's never missed, which I say quietly in case they hear me. Question though: does anyone know if the extra-bags rule counts if the bags are just full of storm-wet cardboard from a trampoline box? Asking for a household that bought a trampoline the week before a storm.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Grown man timing a bin lorry on his watch. Mind you, three weeks is a joke, I'll give you that. Our dealership skip got taken while the car it was next to got left, so they're not perfect anywhere.

units.title: Night crossings cut 'for a crew welfare review'. What does that actually mean?
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Notice went up this morning. Last boat out of Port Ammet now 20:15, the 23:40 and the 00:55 back from Gilliver are gone 'until further notice'. Half my building works late shifts at the hospital. That's management speak for staff shortages, surely. You don't cut sailings to review welfare, you cut sailings because nobody's turned up to crew them.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Possibly, Ewan. What would we expect to see if it were a pure shortage? Usually a cancellation notice night by night, not a fixed timetable change. A fixed change suggests they've decided something about the night roster as a whole. That could be rest hours after a storm week, or it could be the slipway reports. I'd not guess which.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking questions here but has anyone noticed the night sailings are the ones that pass closest to the Holm? Coincidence that they get cut the same month a secretive company is stripping an island nobody's allowed on? I'm not saying anything. Do your research. I have a mailing list if anyone wants the timeline I've put together.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: Every Gilliver sailing passes the Holm, day or night. It's on the way. The daytime ones go just as close.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: I can confirm the night crossings are reduced for a crew welfare review. That is the wording and it is accurate. I won't add to it, and I'd ask people not to guess at individual crew. Daytime sailings are running and the late afternoon boats will be busier, so allow time at the terminal. Logged it, carried on.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Fair enough, skipper, and not aimed at you. But the 20:15 was standing room only tonight. Two lads from the hospital kitchens slept at a mate's in Port Ammet rather than miss it. 'Until further notice' with no date is the bit that grates. Reviews have end dates, normally.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: Ewan, I quite understand the frustration, but the crew are mostly Lisle and Gilliver people, and several of them I taught. If their employer says it's about welfare, I'm inclined to take it at its word for now. Also, a small point: 'nobody's turned up to crew them' should be 'nobody has turned up', in writing.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Noted, Mrs Hale. And fair point about the crew. I'll keep my grumbling for the timetable.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Lisle pier was very quiet tonight without the late boat, I don't think I've locked up at nine in about four years. ha, anyway. Felt odd. I kept looking at the slip out of habit... the lights on it are fine now, the storm only took one bulb.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A reminder that this board is for ferry and road information. Speculation about named crew members, or about why they might need a welfare review, will be removed. Theories about the Holm belong in the Holm thread, with sources please. Thank you. Pell (admin).

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Practical question: does anyone know if the 20:15 connects with the last Tollinby bus at the Port Ammet stand? My sister does lates at the care home on Lisle and is now trying to work out whether she can get home at all on her late days, or whether she has to stay over.

units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Last Tollinby bus leaves the stand 21:05 so yes if the boat's on time. If it's late, and it will be because they're packing it now, the driver usually waits 5 min if you ask nicely at the start of the week. Doesn't help the Gilliver lot coming back though, that last return's gone completely.

units.title: Kittering Holm: the 1953 relay plan, with sources.
units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Since people keep mentioning an 'old plan' for the Holm: it exists, and it is boring. The council archive holds a 1953 Lights Board consultation (ref LB/53/07) for an unattended relay light on the northern knoll. The Courier archive has the announcement and the 1954 note saying it wouldn't go ahead. The History Society has the survey. Links above. Please read them before attaching anything to them.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Thank you for this. The society's article on the relay is linked above; it was a stub until this morning. One correction to the common story: the concrete pillar on the knoll is a survey trig point, not a foundation, and nothing was ever built. The survey copy we hold was donated by an assistant surveyor's family. [citation needed on the pillar's date, I'm afraid.]

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Read section 4 of the survey though. 'The party asked to be taken off before dusk each evening.' Grown men with a government job refusing to sleep on the island. And then the whole project gets dropped with no reason given. Now a holding company buys it through an intermediary and wants every tree gone in a month. Draw your own conclusions, I'm just putting the documents side by side.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: The reason is given, in the same report: staffing. The Board was closing lights in the fifties. As for the survey party, read the next sentence: the boat hire was costed and no time was lost. People who are paid by the day and have a dry bed in Gilliver tend to prefer it to a tent in November. Side by side is not the same as connected.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if the survey party had been frightened? I'd expect them to leave early, or for the report to be cut short. Instead they did fourteen days, took bearings to two lights and costed a tower. That's a job done properly by people who liked their supper.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Aye, well. My grandad's brother was one of the boatmen on that, rowed them across and back every day. Never said much about it except they paid well and he was glad to be home for his tea. Nobody stops over on the Holm, it's not a thing folk do. Not because of anything. Just because.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Finding 1: The 1953 consultation lists the Holm's owner at the time as a Lisle family trust. Finding 2: The trust sold to a timber merchant in 1961. Finding 3: the merchant's heirs sold to the intermediary 18 months ago, as I posted earlier. So the Lights Board never owned it, it only surveyed it. I may be wrong on the 1961 date; the registry scan is faint.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Ledger, the 1961 sale is right; I've seen the conveyance reference. The 'timber merchant' was a sawmill in Tollinby that never cut a stick on the Holm, as far as the record shows. It sat as an asset for sixty years. That is the interesting part, if anything is.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Still nothing back from Grieve about subcontract on the Holm, sent my tickets twice. A lad I know says they're paying well but you can't leave once you're out there, boat comes when it comes. Might just do storm work round tollinby instead, plenty of it this week.

units.author: ex_grieve_corran
units.text: Davey. Do the storm work. I'm not saying anything about this job, I don't know this job. But the boat comes when it comes is how it was up north as well. I won't go into it.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Up north meaning Corran? You keep saying you won't go into it. Then why post at all? Nobody's going to sack you for telling the truth, you don't work there any more. The people on that island deserve to know what they've signed up for.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Gil, please don't badger individual members for information they've chosen not to give. If a member edits or withdraws something, that is their right. This thread is about the relay documents. Thank you.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: I have a copy of a little Lights Board history in the shop, the sort with fold-out maps and a smell of damp. It mentions the Holm in a single line, under 'surveys not proceeded with', between a breakwater and a fog signal. There is something consoling about being a footnote. I will put it in the window if anyone wants to look.

units.title: Carrow Point station: daily readings.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: 20:00 readings. Pressure 1009.8 hPa and climbing. Wind WNW 4 knots, gusts 9. Temperature 6.1 C, dew point 3.4 C. Visibility 30 km plus, you can see the Lisle pier lights with the naked eye. Sky clearing fully. Expect radiation frost inland. Lovely evening for it, if you like that sort of thing, which I do.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thanks for these, they're really useful for us. Quick question: how much salt does a storm like that leave on things near the coast? Garvey says after a big westerly you can taste it on the insulators. I tried. He was joking. I'd still like to know the actual answer.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Ha, good for you for trying. Rough answer: I wipe a glass slide on a post by the station after storms. This one left a visible crust on the windward side, the heaviest since last winter. Rain washes it off higher up, but anything sheltered keeps it. A dew-heavy calm night after a storm is when it causes trouble, as you probably know.

units.title: Lost & Found: storm edition.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Please post lost and found items from the storm here. Bins, gates, trampolines, sheds, small boats. Describe the item and roughly where it was found. A reminder that Pebble the cat was found safe some days ago, so please stop messaging the owner about grey cats. Thank you.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: Found: one blue recycling lid with '14' painted on it in white, in the car park behind Market Row. I've propped it against the wall by the noticeboard. Also one child's yellow wellington, left foot, size small, on the same wall.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Ha, thank you Pell, and thank you everyone who messaged, it was kind. Pebble is fine and spent the whole storm under my duvet. Found: a florist's bucket, galvanised, outside the market hall. It may well be mine, but if anyone else is missing one, it's by my back door.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Lost: one trampoline net, black, about four metres of it, last seen heading east over Orchard Close. The trampoline is fine. The net has gone on to better things. If found, please don't bring it back, we'll be keeping the trampoline in the garage until spring.

units.title: night sailings off from tonight
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Sound Lines bulletin reposted for the lads that don't read it. last sailing from Ammet 20:15, no 23:40, no 00:55 back. until further notice. crew welfare review is the wording. it's their business so keep it civil, these are our own people. take the gossip to the Sound Board.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: For anyone wondering, the review is real paperwork, I've seen the form. Rest hours, fatigue, who's done how many nights back to back. Storm week meant some of us did a lot. Engine room is fine, the generators have never been happier, they love a review, it means they get a night off too.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: I'll say this once since people keep asking me on the quay. I'm fine. I've said what I saw on the slipway and it hasn't changed: end of the slip where the water starts, dark coat, no light, too tall for a kid, didn't answer two hails. The review isn't about me and I'm not the one who asked for it.

units.author: deckhand_finn
units.text: not in the mood for it today lads tbh. day boat's packed and everyone wants to ask the deckie what's going on like I'm going to know. I don't. I coil ropes.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: fair enough Finn. lads leave him be. anyone wanting the timetable read the bulletin.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Rook. For the record, the harbour office has nothing to add about Sound Lines' review and it would not be appropriate for me to comment on it. My slipway notice stands as written: byelaw 14, working areas, no loitering after dark. Please also note the loose stones on the lower slip after the storm. Thank you.

units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Seth has it about right. I'm on days for the time being, which my knees are glad of. The boat is the same boat. If anyone on the late run needs a word, they know where I am. Logged the change, carried on.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Kerris you don't owe anyone anything. For what it's worth, mine at Lisle was the same... still, at the very end, no light. I've stopped saying it was a fisherman because I went and looked at where I'd have had to be standing and you can't fish from there.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Doesn't change much for us, we're in by dark this time of year. Bit quieter on the water at night without the ferry, mind. You get used to her lights coming round the point.

units.title: storm damage, moorings and prices
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: chandlery open 7 till 6. I've got rope, shackles and fenders in. yes I've put the price of 16mm up, so has everyone, it's the supplier not me. three moorings in the outer harbour dragged, the HM's tender is checking them today. green rowing boat still missing.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Mooring check complete. Numbers 31, 33 and 40 have dragged and will be re-laid before any boat goes back on them. Owners have been contacted. The east cardinal at Lisle Spit is also off station, as per the Coastguard notice. Please do not tie up to the visitors' pontoon overnight until the chains are checked. Thank you.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Lost eleven creels on the Holm side, the strings just went. The rest came up full of weed and one very cross lobster. Price at the merchant's was down again yesterday, no lorries got through. Going out first light to look for the rest.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Bram, I can lend you the spare grapnel off the workboat if it helps. Also the merchant's lorry got stuck behind the beech at Mill Bridge, I saw it on the way in. So it's not the price falling, it's the price sitting in a lay-by.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Ta Seth. Found seven of the eleven with the grapnel. Four are on the Holm shore at the north end, I could see the floats from the boat, but I'm not going in there for four creels with the tide where it is. They'll keep.

units.title: storm call-outs
units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: Fourth night out of the last five. Two poles down on the Brackwater ridge, a whole flaming ash tree through the line by the reservoir, and some genius on Holly Lane who tried to move a live drop cable with a garden rake. He's fine. The rake isn't. Ridge is back on. Going to sleep for a week.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: For the record the rake man was very apologetic and gave us a flask. I learned more this week than in my whole first month: how to splice in the rain, how to read a sagged span, and that Garvey sings when he's on a ladder and denies it after.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Garvey you owe me a pint from the bushing argument, and now I owe you one for keeping the terminal's lights on through the storm. Call it even and both buy one. Rest up.

units.author: lineman_garvey
units.text: I don't sing. I hum, which is a safety thing, keeps me breathing steady. Tess, put the gloves in to dry tonight or you'll regret it at six. Gilliver feeder held all storm, by the way, not a single trip. Funny old line, that one, it always does the opposite of what you'd think.

units.title: Housekeeping: storm week, and a note on new threads
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: a few members in the Sound region have had a rough storm week, so be kind if they're short with you. Second, please search before starting another thread about figures at the edge of lights; there are three running. Lamp Hours is company on the night shift, not campfire stories. Drink some water. Ines.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Seconding the water. Also: if you're on your fourth night in a row, your peripheral vision is doing roughly half the work it was on night one, and your brain fills the rest. That's not a ghost, that's a body asking for a nap. N of 1, but I've watched it happen on our monitoring screens.

units.title: New camera, same corner
units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Log, tonight. 00:35 monitor 4 (the new unit, fitted yesterday) shows a person standing at the boundary of the floodlit stack area, northeast corner. 00:36 radioed foot patrol. 00:41 patrol at the corner, nil found. 00:42 monitor 4 still shows the figure in the same spot while patrol stands about four metres from it. Patrol saw nothing. Different camera, same corner. Patrolled, nil found.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Two questions, kindly meant. Is the new camera on the same mount and the same cable run as the old one? If the old fault was in the run or the recorder rather than the camera, swapping the camera changes nothing. And was the patrol visible on monitor 4 at the same time as the figure?

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Same mount, same cable, same recorder. Fair point. Patrol was visible on monitor 4, yes. Both on screen at once, him walking, it standing. I've saved the clip and asked IT to look at the recorder. Patrolled again 01:30, nil found.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: That's the bit that would get me, both on screen together. When we get ghosting it's a smear where someone used to be, and it fades in a few frames. A thing that holds still for six minutes while your patrol walks past it isn't ghosting in any system I've used. Doesn't mean it's anything else. Control says hi, by the way, he reads this.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Rolls are out of the oven at four if you want to come and look at something warm and ordinary, gate 7. Poppy seed tonight, the good ones. I always think a log reads better with a roll beside it.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Here's my worry. A week ago this was 'something on the monitor'. Then it was 'someone at the edge of the lot'. Tonight it's 'it, standing'. Same events, the words get bigger. I'm not saying gate7 is making it up, his logs are the most boring thing on this site, which I mean as praise. I'm saying watch the words.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Fair. Corrected for the log: a figure. Not 'it'. I'll stick to the word on the incident form, which is 'unidentified shape, stationary'. Patrolled 02:10, nil found. Rolls collected.

units.title: the forecourt guy
units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: regular customer update. there's a man who stands outside at the edge of the forecourt light most nights. not in the light. at the edge. never comes in. last night 03:40 to about 04:15. I waved. he didn't. I sold eleven hot dogs and a phone charger. business as usual.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: ok I'm the one who buys the cold coffee at 3 and I've seen him too!! he's just a guy waiting for a lift probably. there's a bus stop on the other side of the road and no shelter so people stand near the shop to keep out of the wind. anyway chapter 4 is due in nine days and I have written the title.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: the bus stops at 23:50 and 05:30. nobody waits four hours for the 05:30. also the title of chapter 4 is very good, I saw it on your laptop.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: At the edge of the light. Again. I've been saying this for weeks... different countries, same distance, same stillness. The people who know aren't going to tell you. I'll leave it there, I've said too much already.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: You haven't said anything, which is the trouble. You never say where, when, or who. Taro has given a time, a place and a bus timetable. That's a report. Yours is a mood. Also: people stand at the edge of light because the middle of it is where they can be seen. That's not hidden knowledge, that's human.

units.title: Break room: what's on your break tonight?
units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Quiet ward tonight, touch wood. Break is a yoghurt that expired yesterday (living dangerously) and the crossword from last week's paper because nobody recycles in the staff room. Seven down has defeated three shifts of nurses now. What's everyone else eating? Back to it in ten.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text:
kebab from the place by the hospital rank, the one where the owner's dad does the onions and argues with the radio
had a fare tonight who wanted to go to the airport and then halfway there remembered his passport was in the other jacket
so we went back and then to the airport
best fare of the week anyway

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Toast, sorry, it's always toast. Mrs A. is awake and wants hers with the crusts on today, which is new, and she says it's because she's 'getting her strength up'. The door intercom has been quiet since the electrician dried out the box. I keep listening for it at ten past three anyway. Sorry, long post for a toast answer.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Protein bar that tastes of cardboard and ambition. Target went up again tonight, 210 lines an hour, because 'we beat it last week'. Yes, because of the storm half the night shift couldn't get in and the rest of us ran. Scanner's behaving at least. No pings from empty aisles since the pallet thing.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Crusts on is a good sign. Ours like a request, it means they're planning ahead. Glad the intercom has settled; mine's been well behaved since they swapped the button. Seven down is 'lamplighter', apparently, a porter from downstairs got it. Back to it.

units.title: Brackwater group session: tonight's the calm one
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Storm's through and the forecast is flat calm, so we go again tonight. Same positions as before: me at the dam path with two omnis and the dish, tern at the pumping house, Odile with the binaural head on the reservoir road halfway between. Clocks synced to the radio signal at 22:00, all of us, and I'll check them again at the end. Paths below the dam are flooded, so stay on the road. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I'm in. new batteries in everything, the spare recorder is charged, and I've printed the sync sheet so we can all write the offset by hand. after last time I'm not trusting anything with a clock on it. also bringing soup. ok so it's tomato, that's all we had.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Useful night to go: after three days of rain the reservoir is at 97 per cent and the overflow may run. If it does, the outflow pipe at the dam foot will be carrying a lot more water than usual. If water hammer is behind any of the knocks, tonight is when it'll be loudest. Please log the spillway condition on the hour.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones on for this one later! I've wrapped the binaural head in a fleece hat, so if you see a small person in a bobble hat on a tripod on the reservoir road, that's Gerald. He's my best ears. I'll mark the left-right axis to the dam so we can compare directions afterwards.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: You'll stay on the road like you've said and you'll be off the estate by four. The paths under the dam are closed for a reason, and the water's up. I'll be doing my round at eleven and I'll want to see you all where you say you are. And no fires.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Understood, and thank you. We'll be on the road, off by four, no fires. You're welcome to listen on the headphones when you come by at eleven, if you want.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Good luck tonight. Reminder for everyone following along: raw files only when you post results, please, and the sync sheet as a photo. No phone recordings of your speakers, no music, no 'enhanced' versions. LowBand is for recordings, not stories.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Good luck to you all tonight, young man. I shall be listening to my old reservoir tape again this evening for comparison, though I remain of the view that what I have is the dam's sluice gear being worked. Do wear proper gloves; the damp gets into the fingers before you notice. Regards, Ned.
units.title: For tonight's session: my old reservoir tape, for comparison
Re-uploads: a final warning
units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: NightScreamLive, this is a final warning. You re-uploaded dunlin_rec's and tern.audio's session files with music and a 'creepy filter' to your channel, after being asked twice not to. Their files are their files. If it happens again you'll be temp-banned. This thread is locked; reply by message if you want to discuss it.

units.title: Stairwell (new thread): please read before posting
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: The old stairwell thread is locked and staying locked. This one is open on three conditions: no naming neighbours, no arguing about whether other people are lying, and stick to what you saw or heard yourself. Kerrow still say the relay part is 'on order'. I've rung them again. Bev, DCRA.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Correction to my earlier count, posted here because the old thread is locked. 1. I recounted Benedikt's file at half speed with headphones. 2. Footsteps after he stops: n=41, not 43. Two I had counted were his own bag knocking the rail. 3. Expected for a two-flight descent: 38 (19 per flight). 4. Excess: 3, not 5. The conclusion stands, smaller.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Credit for publishing the correction. Three excess impulses in a concrete stairwell is well within what a single reflection off the landing above would give you, especially at that time of night with no ambient masking. I'd want to see the excess fall exactly on the flight rhythm before it means anything.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: They fall on the rhythm. Interval 0.58 s, same as his steps, plus or minus 0.02. A reflection would sit at a fixed lag behind each step, not continue after the steps stop. I have checked this. I do not need it to mean anything, I need it to be counted correctly.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: for the record I held the stopwatch for this and Tobin made me redo flight two four times because I breathed. so the 41 is extremely real lol. honestly though. 41 or 43 or whatever, I've been on those stairs at 2am and the bit after you stop is the bit nobody can explain to me.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Thank you Tobin for checking. Yes the bag hits the rail, it is my delivery satchel, I carry it home. Sorry I did not say. I still do not use the stairs. I take the lift and if the lift is broken I wait in the shop with Hassan.

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Thanks Bev. Nothing from us on the stairs, we've stuck to the lift. Still no news from the housing office about the transfer list, they say 'weeks, not days'. R. has a cold and little M. has decided he's not going to school tomorrow. He's six, so we'll see.

units.title: Shop: storm deliveries
units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Bread and milk arrived this morning, first proper delivery in three days, so the shelves are full again. Torches still at cost price, plus batteries. If you can't get down because of the lift, ring the shop and I'll bring it up, no charge for floors 1 to 14. H

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Thank you Hassan. The small rye loaf, if you have one, and I will pay you on Friday as usual. Your nephew carried it up yesterday and refused a biscuit, which I found very worrying in a boy of that age. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Rye is on your door handle, Irena. My nephew is on a diet for football. I have told him a biscuit from a neighbour is not food, it is manners. H

units.title: Car park: the storm is not an excuse
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: During the storm a van parked across bays 12 to 14 for two days. I know it was a storm. I know people needed to get home. But the bays are numbered for a reason. I have written down the registration. I will also say, before anyone asks, that the storm is not a reason to talk about the stairwell in this thread, which is about parking.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: the van was a plumber who fixed the boiler on 4 during the storm, Wendell, he stayed over because the ring road was shut. but yes bays are sacred. I'll tell him you wrote down his registration, he'll be thrilled.
